name: C-130H Hercules
summary: Legacy four-turboprop tactical airlifter, now mostly with Air National Guard and Reserve units as they convert to the C-130J.

wings: High-mounted straight wing with tapered outer panels
Long-span wing above a wide fuselage
engines: Four turboprops with four-blade, paddle-shaped propellers
Some Guard aircraft upgraded with eight-blade straight-bladed propellers
Engine nacelles extend well ahead of the wing leading edge
fuselage: Wide, boxy fuselage with an upswept tail and rear loading ramp
Landing-gear sponsons bulging out along the lower fuselage sides
Small 'eyebrow' windows above the cockpit windscreen; LC-130H often seen on skis
tail: Tall single vertical fin with a dorsal fillet
Large horizontal tail set at the top of the upswept rear fuselage

tellTales: Four-blade paddle propellers on a high-winged four-turboprop
Small eyebrow windows above the cockpit windscreen
Bulging gear sponsons and an upswept tail with rear ramp

confusedWith.howToTell: The C-130H has four-blade paddle props (or eight-blade straight props on some) and eyebrow windows over the cockpit; the C-130J has six-blade curved scimitar props and no eyebrow windows.
